notes: The run is substantively strong (37 accurate, well cross-linked specs, a real implementation gap found and recorded as a dated TODO, clean git tree) and fails on two assertions: prose lint (61 findings, almost all semicolons, which the old skill never asked the executor to run) and the `due_at`/`created_at` leak into tickets.md. Eval critique: the 'behavioral' assertion is the right idea but the field-name boundary is fuzzy; event-log.md legitimately names JSON keys (`kind`, `id`, `at`) because they are on-disk observable, whereas `due_at` is not, so the assertion should say 'identifiers not visible in CLI output or the log file' to make grading deterministic. The invariants assertion says 'one of them' but a good run splits it across INV-001/INV-002; reword to 'the invariants capture'. The placeholder assertion's '...' clause should say 'table cells consisting only of ...' since header text like 'Load when...' is a false-positive candidate. Nothing checks that the documented implementation gap (unknown priority escapes as a traceback) is correct, nor that proposal.md actually flags trade-offs; both are discriminating outcomes this run got right and a weak run would skip.
